output.summary: The yield decline is real: the CMM gauge R&R is stable and Halvard's PPM rose (E4, E5). The new-operator cohort is ruled out, because yield fell before they ran alone and their reject rates match experienced operators (E14). The 12-hour-shift and scrap-tag-timing story is unestablished, because tags are batch-written (E3). Corvane hardness spread and deferred spindle service are both plausible but fully confounded in time, and the machine and lot data cannot separate them (E8, E10, E11, E12). The Line 6 Corvane-on-serviced-lathe data (Q2) and hour-of-machining reconstruction (Q3) would discriminate. Evidence is insufficient to commit to a root-cause fix. Run the staggered spindle service with Tamsworth trials, and do not cut inspection or punish the new operators.
